tagline: Morocco's gateway on the Strait of Gibraltar — Tanger City Port's new marina and cruise basin facing Spain 12 nm across the water, with the coast to Cap Spartel and Tanger Med served today only by road.
summary: Tangier commands the Strait of Gibraltar at the meeting point of the Atlantic and the Mediterranean, one of the world's busiest maritime crossings. Its old harbour has been rebuilt as Tanger City Port, a modern marina, cruise and fast-ferry terminal on the downtown bay, while Tanger Med — Africa's largest port, handling over 10.2M containers and with capacity for ~7M passengers in 2024 — sits ~40 km east. Spain lies just 12 nm across the Strait, with high-speed ferries to Tarifa and Algeciras running frequently. Around the city the Bay of Tangier sweeps from Cap Malabata to Cap Spartel and the Caves of Hercules, a scenic coast linked today only by road. Demand is tourism-, cruise- and cross-border-led and rising with heavy national investment ahead of World Cup 2030. A clean foiling-electric layer fits the sheltered bay transfers (Pioneer II) and the longer coastal and Strait legs (Quanta-LR), and anchors Morocco's Mediterranean gateway for a demand-platform partner. Note: no boarding points are sealed here yet — Tangier is a priority mint candidate.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The sheltered Bay of Tangier legs — city port ↔ Malabata (~3 nm) and ↔ Cap Spartel (~8 nm) — sit well inside the ~70 nm all-electric envelope, with shore charging at the marina basin.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The Tangier ↔ Tanger Med (~24 nm) coastal leg and any Strait crossing run through the exposed, current-swept waters of the Strait of Gibraltar; Quanta-LR's hybrid range and stability make it the right tool for those lines.

competitive_landscape: Today: high-speed conventional ferries across the Strait, road transfers to Tanger Med and around the bay, and the cruise/marina port; no clean fast-passenger service on the local coastal legs.
seasonality: Year-round; Strait currents, wind and swell make a stable foiling hull a clear comfort and safety advantage, especially on cross-Strait and Cap Spartel legs.
regulatory_note: Tanger City Port is operated as a passenger/marina port; Tanger Med under the Tanger Med Special Agency. Cross-Strait services require bilateral Morocco–Spain maritime approvals.
